lead: An optical amplifier boosts light directly, without converting it to electrons. A pump feeds energy into a gain medium, and incoming photons trigger stimulated emission that copies them. It exists because fiber loses about 0.2 dB per km: an 80 km span arrives 16 dB weaker, so eight spans would cost 128 dB. Before amplifiers, every span ended at a receiver and a fresh transmitter started the next. Now one amplifier per span carries the same light across a country or an ocean. EDFAs serve 1550 nm long-haul links; SOAs serve shorter and cheaper links.
prereq: You need Unit 3 (stimulated emission, laser diode) and Unit 2 (attenuation, dB arithmetic); 6.1 explains why one amplifier serves many wavelengths.

sections.h3: Why amplify, and the five numbers

blocks.text: A single-mode fiber at 1550 nm loses about 0.2 dB per km. An 80 km span therefore arrives 0.2 × 80 = 16 dB weaker. Eight such spans lose 128 dB, which no laser can launch and no receiver can detect. An amplifier at each span restores the power, so the same light continues instead of being detected and re-created.

blocks.where: G(dB) is the gain in decibels; P_out is the output power in mW; P_in is the input power in mW. A 20 dB gain means P_out = 100 × P_in.

blocks.text: Five numbers appear on every amplifier data sheet.

items: Gain: 20-40 dB typical; it sets how much span loss one amplifier can pay back.
Gain bandwidth: the wavelength range where gain stays within a stated drop, say 1 dB; the EDFA C-band is about 35 nm wide.
Saturation output power: the output at which gain falls by 3 dB; beyond it the amplifier stops being linear.
Noise figure NF: the dB degradation of signal-to-noise ratio; 3 dB is the theoretical minimum, and lower is better.
Polarization dependence: the gain difference between input polarizations, in dB; it is large in SOAs and small in EDFAs.

blocks.text: A semiconductor optical amplifier (SOA) is a laser diode chip run below threshold. Anti-reflection coatings on both facets stop feedback, so light passes once through the active region and is amplified by stimulated emission. Different material compositions cover 1310 nm and 1550 nm. Gain is 20-30 dB and noise figure 6-8 dB.

Two weaknesses limit its use. Gain depends strongly on polarization, often by several dB, because the active region is asymmetric. Second, the carrier density saturates, so a strong channel reduces gain for its neighbours: cross-gain modulation, which causes crosstalk between WDM channels (see 6.1).

SOAs therefore serve as boosters after a single transmitter, as inline amplifiers in short access links where cost matters more than OSNR, and as gates or wavelength converters, because their gain responds in nanoseconds.

An EDFA is a few metres of silica fiber whose core is doped with Er³⁺ ions, giving a three-level system. A pump photon lifts an ion from level 1 to level 3, which decays quickly to the metastable level 2. A 1550 nm signal photon then stimulates the 2 → 1 transition, adding an identical photon. Pumping at 980 nm reaches level 3; pumping at 1480 nm reaches level 2 directly. The 980 nm pump gives the lower noise figure, 1480 nm the higher saturation power.

The parts are a pump laser, a WDM coupler that merges pump and signal, 10-30 m of doped fiber, isolators before and after to block backward amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) and reflections, and a gain-flattening filter that equalises channels across the band. The C-band runs 1530-1565 nm with 30-40 dB gain and NF 4-6 dB; a longer doped fiber extends gain to the L-band, 1570-1610 nm.

blocks.where: OSNR is the optical signal-to-noise ratio in a 0.1 nm reference bandwidth at 1550 nm; P_in is the power into each amplifier in dBm; NF is its noise figure in dB; N is the number of identical amplifiers in the chain. The constant 58 folds in the reference bandwidth and photon energy.

blocks.text: Every amplifier adds ASE, so noise accumulates while the chain holds signal power fixed. That is why OSNR falls as 10 log₁₀ N: eight amplifiers cost 9.0 dB. Raman amplification, a distributed alternative that pumps the fiber itself, belongs to Unit 2.

figure.caption: The 980 nm pump joins the 1550 nm signal in the WDM coupler, excites the erbium ions in the doped fiber, and the isolator and filter clean the output. The gain medium and pump are the two parts that do the work.

examples.question: A 10 Gb/s channel enters each EDFA at −20 dBm. Every amplifier gives 20 dB gain with a noise figure of 5 dB, and there are 8 spans. (a) Show that the input power to every amplifier is the same. (b) Estimate the OSNR after the last amplifier in 0.1 nm using OSNR = 58 + P_in − NF − 10 log₁₀ N.
steps: Each span loses 20 dB and each amplifier restores 20 dB, so the net change per span is 0 dB. Every amplifier therefore receives −20 dBm.
Compute the chain penalty: 10 log₁₀ 8 = 9.0 dB.
Substitute in OSNR = 58 + P_in − NF − 10 log₁₀ N = 58 − 20 − 5 − 9.0 = 24.0 dB.
10 Gb/s at a bit error rate of 10⁻¹² needs roughly 15-16 dB, so 24.0 dB clears it with about 8 dB margin.
examples.answer: Every amplifier input is −20 dBm, and the OSNR after 8 spans is 24.0 dB, with 9.0 dB of the loss coming from noise accumulation.
examples.check:
import math
N = 8
P_in = -20.0
NF = 5.0
penalty = round(10 * math.log10(N), 1)
osnr = round(58 + P_in - NF - penalty, 1)
print(penalty)
print(osnr)

traps: An amplifier is not a regenerator: it restores power but not pulse shape, so dispersion and jitter pass straight through.
Noise adds up: N identical amplifiers drop OSNR by 10 log₁₀ N, not by a fixed amount per amplifier.
Do not swap noise figure and saturation power; NF is about the weak input end, saturation about the strong output end.
The EDFA gain band is 1530-1565 nm, not the whole low-loss window from 1260 to 1625 nm.
SOA polarization dependence is several dB, not zero; assuming zero gives wrong crosstalk and gain budgets.

quiz.q: Define gain in dB for an optical amplifier.
quiz.a: G(dB) = 10 log₁₀(P_out / P_in); 20 dB means P_out = 100 P_in.

quiz.q: Name the two common EDFA pump wavelengths.
Why does an SOA need anti-reflection coatings on its facets?
quiz.a: To stop facet feedback and lasing, so light makes a single amplified pass.

quiz.q: Why is an EDFA noise figure lower than an SOA noise figure?
quiz.a: The erbium gain medium has no carrier-density noise; EDFA NF is 4-6 dB against 6-8 dB for an SOA.

quiz.q: A span loses 10 dB, the amplifier gain is 23 dB, and the input is −18 dBm. Find the output power.
quiz.a: Output = −18 + 23 = +5 dBm. The 23 dB gain multiplies power by about 200.

quiz.q: By how much does OSNR fall when the chain grows from 1 amplifier to 16 identical amplifiers?
quiz.a: 10 log₁₀ 16 = 12 dB fall, since each stage adds the same ASE.

quiz.q: P_in = −22 dBm, NF = 6 dB, N = 4. Estimate OSNR in 0.1 nm at 1550 nm.

beyond: Not for the exam. Real long-haul systems combine EDFAs with Raman pumping and dynamic gain equalisation, and modern line cards carry per-channel power control. Research pushes the L-band, few-mode erbium-doped fiber for space-division multiplexing, and erbium-doped waveguide amplifiers on silicon photonics. Search for optical signal-to-noise ratio, gain flattening, and erbium-doped waveguide amplifier to go further.
